This is my trick for cheap garden\potting soil, since Miracle Grow potting soil is 10 bucks a bag now. For dirt...

This will triple the volume of dirt you get, give your plants light aerated soil that holds onto moisture, and mix in stuff that your plants will like. Cost is about $30, and the 2 main ingredients will last for a few seasons. Here is the Home Depot list:

  • Perlite - grab the biggest bag they have 1ft by 3ft tall, it will last for years. - $12
  • Organic Peat Moss - 3 cu ft, it will last for years - $12
  • Organic Manure - 1 cu ft, just enough for this year - $4

Optional. Only needed if on sale or if your garden dirt really sucks. (Uptight people like middle_path in /justgrowit should avoid these ingredients, they apparently cause convulsions in sustainable organic vegan pod people.)

  • 1.5cu ft bag of PottingSoil, or Miracle Grow if its on sale. $5
  • Feelin rich? Buy some fertilizer too. $5

Time to mix it up. Find a wheelbarrow, tarp, or just a clear spot in the garden. Round up all the pots and planters from last year. Catch any earthworms under the pots and save them for later. The soil in those pots will have composted the roots over the winter, and probably grown some moss and weeds. Pick out the weeds, keep everything else.

  • Soil - Dump the soil from last years planters in the mixin spot, about 1 cu ft. Chop it up with your dirty hoe.
  • Manure - Add a shovel full.
  • Fertilizer - Toss a handfull in.
  • Perlite - Add 2 shovels of perlite.
  • Peat Moss - Add 2 shovels of peat moss.
  • Potting Soil - Add 2 shovels of that expensive dirt.

Beat the pile vigorously with that dirty hoe, until there are no more lumps, or until you feel better. If you have compost or dead plants\stalks from last year, chop them up and throw those in the bottom of the pots and planters to hold moisture. Then fill all the pots and planters back up, drop in some worms for luck, and you are ready to roll.
